name: Qualitative or Quantitative Defects of Emerin

criteria.description: Demonstration of absent or markedly reduced emerin protein expression in muscle or skin biopsy by immunohistochemistry or Western blot
Presence of the clinical triad: early-onset contractures of elbows and Achilles tendons, slowly progressive muscle weakness and wasting, and cardiac conduction defects
Identification of pathogenic variants in the EMD gene by molecular genetic testing
X-linked inheritance pattern or positive family history consistent with Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical triad plus emerin deficiency or pathogenic EMD gene variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by family history and exclusion of other muscular dystrophies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early-onset contractures of elbows and Achilles tendons
searchTerms: early joint stiffness in elbows and heels
contractures of elbows and Achilles tendons

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cardiac conduction defects including atrioventricular block
pathognomonic.notes: May lead to sudden cardiac death if untreated
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems with AV block

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive muscle weakness and wasting predominantly affecting scapulohumeroperoneal muscles
searchTerms: muscle wasting in shoulder, upper arm, and lower leg
progressive muscle loss in specific limb muscles

common.notes: Often reported early in disease course

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness and limited range of motion

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness leading to dyspnea
occasional.notes: May require ventilatory support in advanced stages
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness

occasional.notes: Secondary to muscle weakness and contractures

rare.notes: Uncommon but reported in some cases

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle atrophy and fatty replacement
Echocardiography demonstrating dilated cardiomyopathy and conduction abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in EMD gene (X-linked inheritance)
Absent or reduced emerin protein expression on immunohistochemistry
other: Electrocardiogram showing atrioventricular conduction block and arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily cardiac involvement without skeletal muscle contractures

redFlags: Early-onset joint contractures with muscle weakness
Progressive cardiac conduction defects requiring pacemaker
Family history of sudden cardiac death in young males
references: Emery AEH. Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy: clinical and genetic features. Neuromuscul Disord. 2000.
Bonne G, et al. Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy: clinical and molecular aspects. Neuromuscul Disord. 1999.
